result:
PR #378 is marked ready. The #283 residual is **reading (2), the texel-tie form**: it is the same v-tie rule tracked in #282, not a 16-bit defect and not a precision floor.

A cloud lane had already refuted readings (1) and (3) on master (`docs/lanes/cloud-283`, PR #338). Its conclusion was "texel selection". This session found which selection it is and why:

- **Every differing pixel is an exact tie.** All 34,727 differing pixels across the 20 Volume texture captures sit where a pixel centre lands exactly on a boundary between two texel rows. None are anywhere else. The top three quads have no exact ties, and they differ by 0 px in every format.
- **The existing tie rule predicts every pixel.** The rule from #282 (cloud-282b's binade rule) was fitted on a different quad. Here it gets the direction right on 6,496 of 6,496 tie pixels where the direction can be read. A model built on it reproduces the Y16 golden with 0 of 75,840 pixels different, and the R16B16 golden with 0 differing RGB pixels.
- **The +1 / −1 split is two separate causes, not one noisy rule:**

  | Y16 pixels | Count | Cause | Fix |
  |---|---:|---|---|
  | +1 | 2,070 | The console hardware sends the tie to the lower row | Hunk B: #282's rule, which needs per-vertex texture coordinates in psh.c |
  | −1, plus one +255 wrap | 535 | Our 3D sample path has no `texelTieBias`, so our tie lands just below the boundary. Wherever we pick the lower row, the hardware picks the upper one (0 exceptions). | **Hunk A** |

**Hunk A** is named in NOTES with its prediction legs, ready for `briefs/pshqueue.md`; it is not applied because psh.c is held by lane.fog278. It adds `texelTieBias` to the 3D path at `psh.c:3038-3045`. Modelled pixel by pixel:
- Y16 goes from 2,605 to 2,070 px and R16B16 from 1,110 to 746 RGB px, breaking none. The gain across the suite is at least 5,853 px.
- It is safe on pixels that aren't ties: the smallest margin is 8.7×10⁻⁴ texel, far above float interpolation error.
- It only reaches Volume texture and the nine `Texture_border/3D_BorderTex_*` captures. Those nine are 0 px today, so they are the leg that would refute it.

This complements lane.tie282c's PR #376, which tested the same rule on one row of Texture render target. I wrote to NOTES and the #282 comment which of my weight cells the earlier fit had already covered, and which one is new.

**Not chased:** decoding the 8888 / A8 / DXT1 / palettised formats (their counts come from the Y16 direction map instead), the rule's general form for other triangle layouts, and checking the rule against the 184 captures outside Volume texture.

**Done:** preflight passes with `--allow-tracker`, and `Files:` matches the diff (NOTES.md only). I commented on #283 recommending it close as fixed by #289, with the +1 class moving to #282, and posted the held-out evidence on #282. The scratch scripts are left uncommitted, as the brief asked; NOTES gives the exact geometry, so the result can be reproduced. I also saved one memory: a ±1 split can be two one-signed causes.
